title: A recent 30-year fit gave no clear six-month level forecast gain for two Great Lakes at 1970-2024 issues
abstract: We tested whether a recent 30-year fit improves six-month forecasts for Superior and Michigan-Huron over an expanding fit since 1920. Both linear models used month, current local level and a three-month local change. At 660 issues in 1970-2024, the equal-lake mean reduction in mean squared error was -5.76%. The conditional 95% five-year block interval was -14.34% to +1.16%. Superior and Michigan-Huron had point losses of 3.69% and 7.83%. Thus, removal of older observations gave no clear gain in this test. Twenty-year and forty-year checks also had point losses. Results use revised v2025 data, one simple model and no weather or regulation inputs. They do not establish stable lake dynamics or operational forecast skill. The package includes original code, aggregate evidence, source hashes, a figure and numerical checks. Source records and individual forecasts are retrieved or regenerated outside the signed package.

display.caption: Six-month forecast tests for Superior and Michigan-Huron at 1970-2024 issues. Bars show conditional 95% five-year block intervals. Negative gains mean larger errors from recent fits. The right panel shows cumulative primary loss savings with a fixed total-loss denominator.
